SELECT
  SUM(CASE WHEN sc.country_name = 'Germany' THEN l.net_amount END) AS germany_by_store,
  SUM(CASE WHEN cc.country_name = 'Germany' THEN l.net_amount END) AS germany_by_customer,
  SUM(
    CASE
      WHEN cc.country_name = 'Germany' AND l.channel = 'online'
      THEN l.net_amount
    END
  ) AS the_difference_web_only,
  MIN(l.order_date) AS covered_from,
  MAX(l.order_date) AS covered_to
FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS l
LEFT JOIN contoso_served.dim_store AS s
  ON l.store_key = s.store_key
LEFT JOIN contoso_served.dim_country AS sc
  ON s.country_code = sc.country_code
LEFT JOIN contoso_served.dim_customer AS c
  ON l.customer_key = c.customer_key
LEFT JOIN contoso_served.dim_country AS cc
  ON c.country_code = cc.country_code

value:
Which Germany do you mean? The two readings are 10,256,061.74 USD apart, and nothing in the ontology picks between them, so I won't guess.

• "The German shops' takings" — what was rung up at Contoso's stores standing in Germany: **14,382,768.44 USD**
• "What German customers spent" — what customers whose registered country is Germany paid, wherever they bought it: **24,638,830.18 USD**

What the choice does NOT change: not one cent was sold at a German shop to a customer living elsewhere, so every counter sale in Germany sits in both figures and the shop-by-shop picture is identical either way. The whole difference is 10,256,061.74 USD of web-shop purchases by German residents — the web shop records its country as `--`, a sentinel that is not a place, so those sales can only be placed in Germany through the buyer, never through the store.

Both figures are net of discount, in USD, and cover every order in the data, placed between 2016-05-18 and 2025-12-31. Say "the shops" or "the customers" and I'll hand you that one.

One reading from your question I cannot price at all: revenue shipped to a German address. The data records when an order was delivered, never where.

Two populations, both drawn from all 223,974 sales lines with no date filter and no channel filter. (a) The store reading, 14,382,768.44: the 14,190 lines whose store's `country_code` resolves to country_name 'Germany' through store__trades_in__country — physical-shop lines only, necessarily, since the web shop's store row carries the `--` sentinel. (b) The customer reading, 24,638,830.18: the 25,552 lines whose customer's `country_code` resolves to 'Germany' through customer__based_in__country, spanning both channels. No trading-state restriction, so sales from German shops that have since closed are in both. The `--` sentinel never equals 'Germany', so country.exclusion.sentinel_is_not_a_country never had to drop a row. 2016-05-18 to 2025-12-31 is the extent of the whole fact table as this query measured it, not of the German slice — from step 2, the first German-customer order is 2016-05-19.
